def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-rat:
## Definition

Let $n\ge1$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable at
$x\in\mathbb R^n$, and put $g:=\nabla f(x)$ using the gradient convention of
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]. Let $B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be a
symmetric matrix and let $\Delta>0$. A quadratic model at $x$ is

$$m(p):=f(x)+\langle g,p\rangle+\tfrac12 p^TBp,\qquad p\in\mathbb R^n,$$

with the Euclidean inner product and norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]
and matrix products as in [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]. The
trust-region ball is $\mathcal B_\Delta:=\{p:\|p\|_2\le\Delta\}$. The
predicted reduction of a feasible step $p\in\mathcal B_\Delta$ is
$\operatorname{pred}(p):=m(0)-m(p)$. Its actual reduction is
$\operatorname{ared}(p):=f(x)-f(x+p)$. When $\operatorname{pred}(p)>0$, the
actual-to-predicted reduction ratio is

$$\rho(p):=\frac{\operatorname{ared}(p)}{\operatorname{pred}(p)}.$$

The quantity $\|B\|_2$ means the matrix norm induced by the Euclidean vector
norm, namely the $p=2$ case of [[def-induced-matrix-p-norm]]. It is not required
that $B=\nabla^2f(x)$ in this definition; exact Hessians and symmetric model
approximations are both admitted. The ratio is undefined when predicted
reduction is nonpositive, so an algorithm must use a separately justified
fallback or return a failure status in that case.
def-adaptive-cubic-regularization-model:
## Definition

Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be twice differentiable at $x$, let
$g:=\nabla f(x)$, let $B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric, and let
$\sigma>0$. The cubic-regularized quadratic model is

$$m_\sigma(s):=f(x)+\langle g,s\rangle+\tfrac12s^TBs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|_2^3,\qquad s\in\mathbb R^n,$$

using the Euclidean conventions of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], the
gradient and Hessian conventions of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and
[[def-hessian-and-euclidean-critical-point]], and the induced matrix norm of
[[def-induced-matrix-p-norm]]. Its predicted reduction is
$m_\sigma(0)-m_\sigma(s)$. Define the actual reduction by
$\operatorname{ared}(s):=f(x)-f(x+s)$ and, when the predicted reduction is
positive, define the ratio
$$\rho_\sigma(s):=\frac{\operatorname{ared}(s)}
{m_\sigma(0)-m_\sigma(s)}.$$
When $B=\nabla^2f(x)$, this is the exact-Hessian ARC model; approximation
error in a different $B$ requires separate bounds. The definition alone
gives no convergence or evaluation-complexity guarantee.
lem-natural-logarithm-bounded-by-argumen:
## Statement

For every real $x\ge1$, the natural logarithm of
[[def-natural-logarithm]] satisfies
$$0\le\log x\le x-1\le x.$$
lem-trust-region-subproblem-optimality-a:
## Statement

Let $B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric, let $g\in\mathbb R^n$, and
let $\Delta>0$. Every global minimizer $p_*$ of
$$q(p):=\langle g,p\rangle+\tfrac12p^TBp\quad\text{over }\|p\|_2\le\Delta$$
has a multiplier $\lambda\ge0$ such that
$$ (B+\lambda I)p_*=-g,\qquad B+\lambda I\succeq0,\qquad
\lambda(\Delta-\|p_*\|_2)=0. $$
Conversely, every feasible $p_*$ satisfying these conditions is a global
minimizer. A global minimizer always exists.

The singular hard case is included as follows. Let $\mu$ be the least
eigenvalue of $B$ and $E_\mu$ its eigenspace. If $\mu<0$, $g\perp E_\mu$,
and the solution $p_0$ of
$(B-\mu I)p_0=-g$, $p_0\perp E_\mu$, has $\|p_0\|_2\le\Delta$, then
$$p_*=p_0+z,\qquad z\in E_\mu,\qquad
\|z\|_2^2=\Delta^2-\|p_0\|_2^2$$
is a global minimizer with the singular multiplier $\lambda=-\mu$. If
$\|p_0\|_2<\Delta$, both signs of any chosen nonzero $z$ of the required
length give distinct minimizers.
alg-trust-region-cauchy-step:
## Definition

Input a model of [[def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-ratio]] with gradient
$g$, symmetric model matrix $B$, and
radius $\Delta>0$. If $g=0$, return $p_C=0$ with status `stationary`. If
$g\ne0$, set $c:=g^TBg$ and define
$$\tau:=\begin{cases}
\Delta/\|g\|_2,&c\le0,\\
\min\{\|g\|_2^2/c,\ \Delta/\|g\|_2\},&c>0.
\end{cases}$$
Return $p_C:=-\tau g$ with status `step`. The procedure uses no matrix
factorization and has no iteration loop.
lem-positive-definite-model-has-unique-n:
## Statement

Let $B$ be the real symmetric positive-definite model matrix of
[[def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-ratio]], with $n\ge1$ and
$g\in\mathbb R^n$. Positive definiteness and invertibility use
[[def-definite-and-indefinite-hessian-quadratic-forms]] and
[[def-invertible-euclidean-linear-map]]. Then there is a unique
$p_N\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfying $Bp_N=-g$.
lem-global-cubic-model-minimizer-decreas:
## Statement

For the cubic model $m_\sigma$ of [[def-adaptive-cubic-regularization-model]],
with $\sigma>0$ and symmetric $B$, a global minimizer exists. If $g\ne0$ and
$s_*$ is any global minimizer, then $s_*\ne0$ and
$$g+Bs_*+\sigma\|s_*\|_2s_*=0,$$
$$m_\sigma(0)-m_\sigma(s_*)\ge\frac{\sigma}{6}\|s_*\|_2^3.$$
lem-trust-region-cauchy-decrease:
## Statement

In the quadratic model of [[def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-ratio]],
let $g\ne0$, let $B$ be symmetric, and let $\Delta>0$. Write
$M:=\|B\|_2$ for the induced Euclidean matrix norm, with the convention
$\min\{\Delta,\|g\|_2/M\}=\Delta$ when $M=0$. The Cauchy step
$p_C$ of [[alg-trust-region-cauchy-step]] minimizes the model on the
negative-gradient segment $\{-tg:0\le t\le\Delta/\|g\|_2\}$ and satisfies
$$m(0)-m(p_C)\ge\tfrac12\|g\|_2
\min\{\Delta,\|g\|_2/M\}.$$
alg-dogleg-trust-region-step:
## Definition

Input a quadratic trust-region model of
[[def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-ratio]] with positive-definite $B$
([[def-definite-and-indefinite-hessian-quadratic-forms]]) and radius
$\Delta>0$. If $g=0$, return $p=0$ with status `stationary`. Otherwise
compute the Cauchy step $p_C$ by [[alg-trust-region-cauchy-step]] and the
unique Newton-model step $p_N$ solving $Bp_N=-g$, whose existence and
uniqueness are established in
[[lem-positive-definite-model-has-unique-newton-step]].

1. If $\|p_N\|_2\le\Delta$, return $p_N$.
2. If $\|p_C\|_2=\Delta$, return $p_C$.
3. Otherwise put $d:=p_N-p_C$, $a:=\|d\|_2^2$,
   $b:=2\langle p_C,d\rangle$, and $c:=\|p_C\|_2^2-\Delta^2<0$. Compute
   $$t:=\frac{-b+\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}.$$
   Here $a>0$ because $p_N\ne p_C$, and the polynomial
   $\|p_C+td\|_2^2-\Delta^2$ is negative at $t=0$ and positive at $t=1$.
   Its two roots have product $c/a<0$, so exactly one is positive and it
   lies in $(0,1)$. Set $p_D:=p_C+td$, the boundary intersection on the
   segment from the Cauchy step to the Newton-model step.
4. Compare the two model values. Return $p_D$ if $m(p_D)\le m(p_C)$ and
   return $p_C$ otherwise.

The status is `step` in the nonstationary branches. The procedure uses one
linear solve and a scalar quadratic root; it has no iteration loop.
alg-truncated-cg-trust-region-step:
## Definition

Input a model of [[def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-ratio]], a finite
inner cap $J\in\mathbb N_0$, and a
residual tolerance $\tau_{tol}\ge0$. If $g=0$, return $0$ with status
`stationary`. Otherwise initialize $z_0=0$, $r_0=g$, $d_0=-r_0$, and $j=0$.
For at most $J$ inner iterations:

1. If $\|r_j\|_2\le\tau_{tol}$, take $z_j$ as the candidate and stop.
2. If $d_j=0$, take $z_j$ as the candidate and stop; the final comparison
   below then returns $p_C$ whenever $z_j$ does not give at least its model
   decrease.
3. Put $c_j:=d_j^TBd_j$. If $c_j\le0$, set
   $$t_j:=\frac{-\langle z_j,d_j\rangle+
   \sqrt{\langle z_j,d_j\rangle^2+\|d_j\|_2^2(\Delta^2-\|z_j\|_2^2)}}
   {\|d_j\|_2^2},$$
   take $z_j+t_jd_j$ as the candidate, and stop. This is the nonpositive
   curvature boundary exit.
4. Otherwise put $\alpha_j:=\|r_j\|_2^2/c_j$ and
   $\widehat z:=z_j+\alpha_jd_j$.
   If $\|\widehat z\|_2\ge\Delta$, use the same positive-root formula in
   step 3, take $z_j+t_jd_j$ as the candidate, and stop at the trust boundary.
5. Set $r_{j+1}:=r_j+\alpha_jBd_j$ and $z_{j+1}:=\widehat z$. If
   $\|r_{j+1}\|_2\le\tau_{tol}$, take $z_{j+1}$ as the candidate and stop.
   Otherwise set
   $$\beta_{j+1}:=\frac{\|r_{j+1}\|_2^2}{\|r_j\|_2^2},\qquad
   d_{j+1}:=-r_{j+1}+\beta_{j+1}d_j,$$
   and increase $j$ by one.

If the cap is reached, take the current feasible $z_j$ as the candidate. In
all nonstationary cases compute the Cauchy step $p_C$ and compare model values:
return the candidate if its model value is no greater than $m(p_C)$, and
otherwise return $p_C$. Thus a capped or unhelpful inner recurrence still
returns an explicit feasible step. A positive boundary root exists in steps 3
and 4 because every non-exit iterate is strictly inside the ball, the
direction is nonzero after the zero-direction guard, and
$\|z_j+td_j\|_2^2-\Delta^2$ is negative at $t=0$ and tends to $+\infty$ as
$t\to+\infty$.
Every recurrence vector $z_j$ lies in the Krylov subspace
$K_j(B,-g)$ of [[def-krylov-subspace-of-a-matrix-and-start-vector]].
alg-adaptive-cubic-regularization:
## Definition

Input an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, a twice continuously
differentiable $f:U\to\mathbb R$, an initial point $x_0\in U$, target
$\varepsilon\ge0$, outer trial cap $N\in\mathbb N_0$, and an exact-Hessian
cubic-model solver $S$. On an input model and finite inner cap $J\in\mathbb N$,
$S$ returns either `no-candidate` or a global minimizer of that model; the
solver is permitted to return `no-candidate` if it cannot certify a minimizer
within its cap. Other inputs are $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$,
$\gamma_{up}>1$, $0<\gamma_{down}<1$, $0<\kappa<1$,
$0<\sigma_{min}\le\sigma_0\le\sigma_{max}$, and the inner cap $J$.
The output is the last accepted iterate and one of `stationary`,
`target-achieved`, `outer-budget-exhausted`, `model-solver-failure`,
`inconsistent-model-solver`, or `regularization-cap-exhausted`.

For $k=0,1,\ldots,N$, in order:

1. Compute $g_k:=\nabla f(x_k)$. If $g_k=0$, return $(x_k,\texttt{stationary})$.
   If $\|g_k\|_2\le\varepsilon$, return $(x_k,\texttt{target-achieved})$.
   If $k=N$, return $(x_k,\texttt{outer-budget-exhausted})$.
2. Set $B_k:=\nabla^2 f(x_k)$ and form the model
   $m_k(s)=f(x_k)+\langle g_k,s\rangle+\tfrac12s^TB_ks+
   \tfrac{\sigma_k}{3}\|s\|_2^3$ of
   [[def-adaptive-cubic-regularization-model]]. Call $S(m_k,J)$. If it returns
   `no-candidate`, return $(x_k,\texttt{model-solver-failure})$. For a
   returned $s_k$, recompute $\operatorname{pred}_k:=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)$. If
   $s_k=0$ or $\operatorname{pred}_k\le0$ while $g_k\ne0$, return
   `inconsistent-model-solver`.
3. Evaluate $f(x_k+s_k)$ and set
   $\rho_k:=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)]/\operatorname{pred}_k$.
   If $\rho_k<\eta_1$, reject the step and keep $x_{k+1}:=x_k$. If
   $\sigma_k=\sigma_{max}$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{regularization-cap-exhausted})$; otherwise set
   $\sigma_{k+1}:=\min\{\gamma_{up}\sigma_k,\sigma_{max}\}$ and continue.
4. If $\rho_k\ge\eta_1$, accept and set $x_{k+1}:=x_k+s_k$. If
   $\rho_k>\eta_2$ and
   $\|s_k\|_2\ge\kappa\|g_k\|_2/\sigma_k$, set
   $\sigma_{k+1}:=\max\{\sigma_{min},\gamma_{down}\sigma_k\}$;
   otherwise set $\sigma_{k+1}:=\sigma_k$.

The model solver is an explicit subroutine input, not a claim that its finite
budget always succeeds. The global-minimizer decrease estimate is supplied by
[[lem-global-cubic-model-minimizer-decrease]]. This procedure alone makes no
unconditional convergence or evaluation-complexity claim.
lem-truncated-cg-iterates-are-krylov-vec:
## Statement

For the interior recurrence of [[alg-truncated-cg-trust-region-step]], before
it exits at the boundary, nonpositive curvature, residual tolerance, or inner
cap, its vectors satisfy
$$z_j\in K_j(B,-g),\qquad r_j,d_j\in K_{j+1}(B,-g),$$
where $K_j$ is the Krylov subspace of
[[def-krylov-subspace-of-a-matrix-and-start-vector]].
alg-trust-region-method:
## Definition

Input $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^1$, an initial point $x_0$,
an initial radius $0<\Delta_0\le\Delta_{max}$, a trial cap
$N\in\mathbb N_0$, a target $\varepsilon\ge0$, constants
$0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, $0<\gamma_{dec}<1<\gamma_{inc}$,
$0<\theta_C\le1$, and a declared model-Hessian bound $M_B\ge0$. At each
trial $k$, the supplied symmetric model matrix $B_k$ must satisfy
$\|B_k\|_2\le M_B$. A finite-budget subproblem routine $S$ returns either a
vector or `failure`; its output is treated only as a candidate and is not
assumed to minimize the trust-region model. The output is the last accepted
point and one of `stationary`, `target-achieved`, `outer-budget-exhausted`,
or `model-evaluation-failure`.

For $k=0,1,\ldots,N$, in order:

1. Set $g_k:=\nabla f(x_k)$. If $g_k=0$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{stationary})$. If $\|g_k\|_2\le\varepsilon$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{target-achieved})$. If $k=N$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{outer-budget-exhausted})$.
2. Form $m_k$ from [[def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-ratio]], compute
   the Cauchy step $p_C$ from [[alg-trust-region-cauchy-step]], and set
   $P_C:=m_k(0)-m_k(p_C)>0$. Query $S$ with this model and radius. Use its
   candidate $q$ only if it is feasible and
   $m_k(0)-m_k(q)\ge\theta_C P_C$; otherwise set $p:=p_C$. If it qualifies,
   set $p:=q$. If $M_B=0$, interpret $\|g_k\|_2/(2M_B)=+\infty$. Whenever
   $\Delta_k\le\|g_k\|_2/(2M_B)$, replace the candidate by $p:=p_C$.
3. Recompute $P_k:=m_k(0)-m_k(p)$. The selection rule ensures
   $P_k\ge\theta_C P_C>0$. Evaluate
   $\rho_k:=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+p)]/P_k$. If this evaluation is unavailable,
   return $(x_k,\texttt{model-evaluation-failure})$.
4. If $\rho_k<\eta_1$, reject: set $x_{k+1}:=x_k$ and
   $\Delta_{k+1}:=\gamma_{dec}\Delta_k$. Otherwise accept and set
   $x_{k+1}:=x_k+p$. If $\rho_k\ge\eta_2$ and $\|p\|_2=\Delta_k$, set
   $\Delta_{k+1}:=\min\{\gamma_{inc}\Delta_k,\Delta_{max}\}$; in every
   other accepted case set $\Delta_{k+1}:=\Delta_k$.

Every trial ratio has a positive denominator. The method retains the last
accepted point; because accepted trials have $\rho_k\ge\eta_1>0$, its
objective value is no greater than any earlier accepted value. The finite
subproblem budget alone does not imply convergence or a complexity bound.
lem-trust-region-ratio-accuracy-for-smal:
## Statement

Let $m$ be the model of
[[def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-ratio]], with $g\ne0$, symmetric
$B$, and radius $\Delta>0$. Suppose $\|B\|_2\le M_B$ for a declared
$M_B\ge0$, and $f$ is $C^1$ on an open set containing the segment from $x$
to $x+p$. Suppose the gradient of $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz on that segment,
meaning
$$\|\nabla f(u)-\nabla f(v)\|_2\le L\|u-v\|_2$$
there. Let $0<\theta\le1$, let $p$ be feasible, and suppose
$$m(0)-m(p)\ge\theta\,[m(0)-m(p_C)]$$
for the Cauchy step $p_C$ of [[alg-trust-region-cauchy-step]]. Interpret
$\|g\|_2/(2M_B)=+\infty$ if $M_B=0$, and assume
$\Delta\le\|g\|_2/(2M_B)$. Then the predicted reduction is positive and
$$|\rho(p)-1|\le\frac{2(L+M_B)\Delta}{\theta\|g\|_2}.$$
Consequently, for $0<\eta_2<1$, if $L+M_B>0$ and
$$\Delta\le\frac{\theta(1-\eta_2)\|g\|_2}{2(L+M_B)},$$
then $\rho(p)\ge\eta_2$. If $L+M_B=0$, then $\rho(p)=1$.
lem-adaptive-cubic-unsuccessful-iteratio:
## Statement

Suppose $f$ is $C^2$ and its Hessian is $L$-Lipschitz on each trial segment,
meaning
$$\|\nabla^2f(u)-\nabla^2f(v)\|_2\le L\|u-v\|_2.$$
Run [[alg-adaptive-cubic-regularization]] with exact Hessians, an exact global
minimizer of each cubic model on every solver-success trial,
$0<\sigma_{min}\le\sigma_k\le\sigma_{max}$, and $\sigma_{max}\ge3L$.
Then no ratio-based rejection occurs when $\sigma_k\ge3L$. If
$\gamma_{up}>1$, let $R\in\mathbb N_0$ satisfy
$\gamma_{up}^R\sigma_{min}\ge3L$; such an $R$ exists. Every block of
consecutive ratio-based rejected trials has length at most $R$.
thm-trust-region-global-liminf-gradient:
## Statement

Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, bounded below, and have an
$L$-Lipschitz gradient on every trial segment. At every iteration let $B_k$
be symmetric with $\|B_k\|_2\le M_B$ for a fixed $M_B\ge0$. Run an infinite
trust-region process of [[alg-trust-region-method]] with no positive target
and no outer cap, fixed $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$,
$0<\gamma_{dec}<1<\gamma_{inc}$, $0<\theta_C\le1$, and
$0<\Delta_0\le\Delta_{max}$. If it does not terminate at a stationary
point, then
$$\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2=0.$$
thm-trust-region-epsilon-iteration-compl:
## Statement

Assume the hypotheses and parameter ranges of
[[thm-trust-region-global-liminf-gradient]], and let $f_{inf}$ be a lower
bound for $f$. For each target $0<\varepsilon\le1$, run
[[alg-trust-region-method]] until its first iterate with
$\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\le\varepsilon$. Define
$$c_\delta:=\min\left\{\frac1{2M_B},
\frac{\theta_C(1-\eta_2)}{2(L+M_B)}\right\},\qquad
c_R:=\min\{\Delta_0,\gamma_{dec}\min\{c_\delta,\Delta_{max}\}\},$$
where a zero denominator means $+\infty$, and put
$$c_P:=\min\{c_R,1/M_B\},\qquad
c_S:=\tfrac12\eta_1\theta_Cc_P>0.$$
Then the number $N_s$ of accepted steps before reaching the target and the
number $N_u$ of rejected trials obey
$$N_s\le\frac{f(x_0)-f_{inf}}{c_S\varepsilon^2},$$
$$N_u\le\frac{\log(\Delta_0/r_\varepsilon)+N_s\log\gamma_{inc}}
{|\log\gamma_{dec}|},\qquad
r_\varepsilon:=\min\{\Delta_0,\gamma_{dec}\min\{c_\delta\varepsilon,
\Delta_{max}\}\}.$$
Here $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm of a positive real.
Consequently, accepted steps and total trials $N_s+N_u$ are
$O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. An outer cap at least
the resulting total-trial bound suffices for the finite-budget algorithm to
return `target-achieved`.
thm-adaptive-cubic-regularization-epsilo:
## Statement

Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$, bounded below by $f_{inf}$, and
have an $L$-Lipschitz Hessian on every trial segment in induced Euclidean
matrix norm. Run [[alg-adaptive-cubic-regularization]] with exact Hessians,
and suppose every model call returns an exact global minimizer. Let
$0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, $\gamma_{up}>1$, $0<\gamma_{down}<1$,
$0<\kappa<1$, and $0<\sigma_{min}\le\sigma_k\le\sigma_{max}$ with
$\sigma_{max}\ge3L$. For any target $0<\varepsilon\le1$, the process
reaches an iterate with $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\le\varepsilon$. Let
$R\in\mathbb N_0$ satisfy $\gamma_{up}^R\sigma_{min}\ge3L$ (take $R=0$
if $\sigma_{min}\ge3L$), and put
$$C_g:=\sigma_{max}+\sqrt n\,L,\qquad
c:=\frac{\eta_1\sigma_{min}}{6C_g^{3/2}}.$$
Then the numbers of accepted steps $N_s$ and rejected trials $N_u$ through
the first target iterate obey
$$N_s\le [f(x_0)-f_{inf}]c^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3/2}+1,\qquad
N_u\le R N_s.$$
Thus the number of trials and each of the function, gradient, and Hessian
evaluation counts are $O(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$. A finite outer cap at least
the resulting trial count suffices for the algorithm to return
`target-achieved`.
